name: PT Kawasan Industri Jababeka Tbk

frontmatter.title: Jababeka: the land is real, the discount is wider than the cycle
frontmatter.summary: KIJA sells industrial land in Bekasi and Kendal and runs the power and water that come with it. The 2026 profit fall is a refinancing charge, not a broken business: the coupon fell and the dollar maturity wall is gone. Land carried at a tenth of achieved prices gives an RNAV far above the share price. We initiate at Buy with a target of Rp184.
thesis: The nine-month profit decline in 2026 is a one-off cost of swapping dollar Senior Notes for a long-dated rupiah facility at a lower coupon, not a deterioration in the land business.

The land bank of 4,443 ha is carried at IDR5,783.5bn while developed industrial land in Cikarang clears at a large multiple of that; we mark it on a monetisation basis with a stated haircut, not on book and not on an appraisal.
Recurring income from power, water and estate services is now the majority of revenue and is still compounding on tenant demand from data-centre, EV-battery and Chinese relocation projects.
Minorities take roughly half of group profit, which is why we keep a wide discount to RNAV rather than assume the land is sold at full value.

catalysts.event: Full-year marketing-sales print for 2026 against the company target
FY2026 audited results, first clean read on the refinanced interest line
Kendal phase-two land conversions and any data-centre tenant announcement

blocks.text: We initiate on PT Kawasan Industri Jababeka at **BUY** with a target of **Rp184**, 54.3% from the Rp120 close [S0]. Our twelve-month value is Rp153 weighted forward and rests on three legs: RNAV at Rp161 carries the most weight, with book value at Rp184 and earnings at Rp99.

The variant view is that the market has read the 2026 profit fall as a deterioration in the business. It is not. Nine-month revenue reached IDR4,254.9bn while consolidated net profit fell to IDR391.7bn, and management attributes the fall to a one-off charge booked in the second quarter when the dollar Senior Notes were refinanced into rupiah bank debt [S3, S4]. That transaction extended the maturity to a fifteen-year tenor, cut the coupon, and removed the currency mismatch that had been generating the swings [S5]. What is genuinely lost is smaller than what is gained: the amortisation and hedging costs are gone for good and the interest bill falls from the level the FY2025 accounts show [S2, S5].

What the market is not paying for is the land. The company holds 4,443 ha of land for development carried at IDR5,783.5bn [S2] against Cikarang developed-land prices of IDR567.4bn for 18.0 ha sold in FY2025 [S2]. We value that land on a monetisation basis, net of the minority's share of the Kendal uplift, and still reach an RNAV per share several times the current price. Two things move the value from here: the marketing-sales run-rate, which was IDR1,520.0bn in the first nine months of 2026 against a full-year target of IDR3,750.0bn [S3, S2], and whether the discount to RNAV returns to its own five-year median from the wider level the shares now trade at.

Three corrections separate this version from the first draft, and all three are in the numbers a reader can rebuild from section four. First, the target discount is now the name's own five-year median of 73.3% on a constant-RNAV basis, not a narrower figure: we could not source a dated re-rating catalyst, and the house macro desk carries the policy rate flat at 5.8 rate percent through FY2027E with IDR property on avoid [deck.macro], so a discount at the bottom of the name's own range would have rested on an assumed rate cut. Second, the land value is net of the minority's share of the Kendal uplift - PT Kawasan Industri Kendal is held 51.0% through a subsidiary with Sembcorp holding the rest [S2] - and that alone moves the published target by several percent. Third, the bear case now shocks the floating rate on the Mandiri facility and holds the discount wider than today's, so the downside case is a real downside case rather than a variant of the base.

Jababeka develops and manages industrial estates and sells the land, factory buildings and residential product inside them. The consolidated accounts report five segments: real estate, golf, service and maintenance, power generation and tourism [S2]. In FY2025 the real-estate pillar produced IDR2,583.0bn of revenue and the infrastructure pillar IDR2,567.0bn, so utilities and estate services are no longer a side-business: management puts recurring revenue at half of the group total, up from two-fifths the year before [S2]. Within infrastructure, power generation is the largest line at IDR1,810.9bn, sold to tenants in Cikarang and Kendal and backed by a take-or-pay capacity arrangement with the state utility while the plant sits in cold reserve [S2].

The footprint is four land banks. Kota Jababeka at Cikarang is the mature township next to Jakarta; Kendal in Central Java is the growth engine, where the company sold 142 ha for IDR2,510.0bn in FY2025 [S2]; Tanjung Lesung in Pandeglang is a tourism estate that has not developed as planned; and Morotai is a greenfield option in the eastern islands [S2]. The land is carried at cost by site in the land note, which we reproduce in the facts file so the reader can see how far carrying value sits below transaction prices [S2].

Strategy is to convert from a land seller into an estate operator: build the water, waste-water, power and logistics infrastructure, keep the recurring fee, and sell land into a tenant base that is increasingly Chinese and increasingly data-centre and EV-battery driven [S2]. The constraint is capital. This is a company that historically funded itself with dollar debt and rolled it, and the 2026 refinancing is the first time it has broken that pattern [S5].

Revenue mechanics are worth spelling out because they drive the forecast. Industrial land is sold plot by plot, often with a building contract, and is recognised when control passes; residential product inside the township follows handover and therefore lags presales; and utility revenue is billed monthly to tenants and grows with occupancy and with the number of connected estates [S2]. That is why the infrastructure pillar can compound while land sales stall, and why the group's reported revenue has been far more stable than its land sales [S2, S3]. The golf course, the convention and tourism assets and the estate-management contract book are small but they explain part of the gap between the segment note and the reported property margin [S2]. Control sits with the founder, who is also president director: insiders hold 40.6% and the free float is 54.9% [S0]. The company employs 713.0 people [S0]. The structure of the growth assets is the most important fact for a shareholder: the Kendal and township developments sit in subsidiaries with significant minority holders, and minorities took roughly half of FY2025 group profit [S2]. Any valuation of the land has to travel through that minority share before it reaches the parent.

Demand for Indonesian industrial estate land has been led by data centres, the EV and battery supply chain, electronics and logistics, and KIJA's own buyer list shows the mix rather than the theme: a Korean personal-care manufacturer taking six hectares, an Indonesian data-centre operator taking four, and in Kendal a Chinese tyre maker, a Chinese building-materials producer and a Chinese synthetic-leather producer [S2]. That is a named pipeline, and it is the reason the infrastructure pillar has compounded at a rate land sales have not [S2, S3].

Competition is increasing in Central Java rather than in KIJA's core. The investment ministry has committed to issuing permits for twelve new industrial estates across the province, including in Kendal and Batang, within a month [S6]. More supply in Central Java caps the price Kendal can hold over time, which is why we do not extrapolate the FY2025 Kendal pricing indefinitely and why the land valuation in section four uses the FY2025 achieved price rather than a higher one.

The moat is location and infrastructure rather than land ownership: Cikarang's estate is infrastructure-connected, has a dry port and a tenant ecosystem, and a buyer of industrial land cannot easily substitute a plot without power, water and permits [S2]. Against that, the company is a price-taker on land, and management says buyers have become more cautious [S3]. Our five-forces read is that supplier power is low, buyer power is rising, substitutes are the new Central Java estates, and rivalry is intensifying - a structure that supports steady volume, not pricing power.

The prices the company actually transacts at tell us where the cycle is. In FY2025 Cikarang developed industrial land sold for IDR567.4bn across 18.0 ha and Kendal for IDR2,510.0bn across 142 ha [S2], which is multiples of the carrying cost per hectare implied by the land note [S2]. That gap is the whole investment case and also its main fragility: a price set by industrial tenants' expansion budgets rather than by replacement cost can move quickly, and the FY2025 mix - one large Kendal tranche, a handful of Cikarang plots - is thin enough that a single cancellation shifts the average. We therefore treat the FY2025 achieved price as the ceiling for our land marking, not as a base from which to grow, and we show in section four what survives a haircut to it.

The macro backdrop matters here more than for most names, because industrial land is a capital-expenditure decision by a manufacturer and therefore rate- and currency-sensitive. The house macro desk has the rupiah under balance-of-payments pressure, IDR rate-sensitive sectors including property on avoid, and the policy rate flat at 5.8 rate percent through FY2027E rather than falling [deck.macro]. We therefore do not underwrite a rate-cut-driven recovery in mortgage or industrial demand: the FY2027 improvement in our forecast comes from the marketing pipeline the company named transaction by transaction in the third quarter [S3] and from the refinancing, not from the policy rate.

Revenue has compounded from IDR2,747.2bn in FY2022 to IDR5,149.4bn in FY2025, but the composition changed more than the total. Real-estate revenue was flat to down as land recognition slipped, while infrastructure revenue grew from IDR1,461.0bn to IDR2,567.0bn [S2]. Gross margin consequently fell to 39.5%, because electricity resale earns a much thinner margin than land [S2]. That mix shift, not pricing, explains most of the margin history, and it caps how far group margin can rise even if land volumes recover.

Our forecast reflects three judgements. First, marketing sales fall to IDR2,412.0bn in FY2026 from IDR3,600.0bn, because the nine-month print of IDR1,520.0bn cannot reach the company's IDR3,750.0bn target and management itself flags buyer caution [S3, S2]. Second, we recognise most contracted land in the year it is signed: the customer-advance balance of IDR1,021.7bn is a small fraction of annual presales, so the recognition lag is short [S2]. Third, recurring revenue keeps growing at a double-digit rate into FY2027 as tenant power demand converts into billings [S3, S2]. On those assumptions FY2026 revenue is IDR5,508.5bn with EBITDA of IDR1,532.8bn and parent net profit of IDR318.9bn, recovering to IDR560.9bn in FY2027 when the one-off is behind us.

The FY2026E base is bridged line by line to the reported nine months, because a forecast that does not reconcile to the last print is an assumption, not a forecast. Revenue of IDR5,508.5bn is the nine-month IDR4,254.9bn plus a fourth quarter below the nine-month quarterly average: land recognition was pulled forward into the third quarter - the property pillar booked IDR1,914.8bn in nine months against IDR974.9bn in the first half alone [S4] - and presales are running a third below last year [S3]. Gross profit of IDR2,026.4bn is the nine-month IDR1,577.8bn plus a fourth quarter at the same margin, which is how the two lines stay consistent. EBIT of IDR1,332.3bn carries a full year of selling and administrative cost at the audited rate of 12.6% of revenue; financial expense of IDR350.1bn is the refinanced debt at the blended rate; financial income of IDR217.3bn is the yield on opening cash; and the other line of IDR-518.0bn carries the Q2 refinancing charge that is already inside the nine months plus its group-level FX and hedge tail [S3, S4]. Group net profit on that build is IDR613.3bn, i.e. the reported IDR391.7bn plus a fourth quarter no weaker than the FY2025 fourth quarter, and parent profit is IDR318.9bn after minorities.

Two cautions on that bridge. The company's own nine-month EBITDA print of IDR1,362.4bn is not on the engine's basis: measured against nine-month gross profit it implies selling and administrative cost of about a twentieth of revenue, against 12.6% in the audited FY2025 accounts [S2], so we bridge on gross profit and net profit and do not lift the forecast to the company's EBITDA figure. And the FY2026E EBITDA margin of 27.8% sits below FY2025's 30.5% because the development gross margin is the nine-month realised rate rather than the FY2025 one - see the next paragraph - not because we expect costs to rise.

The gross-margin history needs the nine-month print in it, because the first draft omitted it. Reported nine-month gross profit of IDR1,577.8bn on revenue of IDR4,254.9bn is a lower group margin than FY2025's 39.5%: gross profit grew by less than a tenth while revenue grew by about a sixth [S3]. The compression is mix, not price. Electricity resale grew by more than half and now supplies the largest single line of recurring revenue, and it earns a margin in the high teens against the low fifties on developed land [S2 note 34], so every point of revenue mix that shifts towards resale costs about a third of a point of group margin. Applying the FY2025 segment margins to the nine-month mix would give a higher group margin than the one reported, which is why we carry 48.3% on the development pillar for FY2026E rather than the FY2025 rate: the realised rate is the evidence. The recurring 27.0% is a floor rather than a waypoint - it assumes no recovery in the electricity tariff spread - and the FY2027E return to the audited development rate is the FY2024 and FY2025 actual, not an expansion beyond it [S2 note 34].

Two restatements of the market data matter. The data pack's depreciation line is a fraction of the real charge: the audited accounts show depreciation and amortisation of IDR187.6bn in FY2025 against the pack's figure, so we rebuild EBITDA and history from the filing [S2, S0]. We do the same for financial expenses, which were IDR420.1bn against the pack's interest line [S2, S0]. Without those restatements EBITDA is understated and the interest and tax lines are inconsistent with the balance sheet.

Cash generation is the strongest part of the record. Operating cash flow exceeded net profit in each of the last two years, so accruals are negative and earnings are backed by cash [S0]. Trade receivables fell while revenue rose, the opposite of the divergence flag we look for [S0]. The balance sheet carries debt of IDR4,606.5bn against equity of IDR6,263.6bn, net debt to EBITDA is 0.6, and the refinancing moved the whole dollar issue into rupiah on a long tenor [S0, S5]. The weakness is the minority leakage: of IDR857.1bn of group net profit only IDR423.2bn reached parent shareholders [S2]. Capital allocation has been conservative on dividends, with a payout of 10.0% [S0, S2].

Related-party gravity is the channel the method card tells us to quantify, so here it is as a share of the group. The parent-company accounts show other receivables from related parties of IDR174.5bn and other payables to related parties of IDR228.0bn at 31 December 2025 [S2 p.573-574]. Those balances are well under a tenth of group revenue of IDR5,149.4bn and under a twentieth of group total assets of IDR15,056.2bn - large enough to monitor, too small to explain the discount on their own. No related-party revenue line is disclosed in the consolidated accounts, which is itself the finding: the flows are financing balances between group companies and affiliates, not sales booked at non-market prices to a controller's other ventures. The auditor is Tanubrata, Sutanto, Fahmi, Bambang and Rekan, a BDO member firm [S2]. The structure flags are real but disclosed: the new bank facility is secured at a stated collateral cover over company and subsidiary assets [S5], and the minority interest of IDR1,880.8bn represents half the economics of the growth subsidiaries, with IDR1,570.1bn of it sitting in Kendal alone [S2 note 24]. None of these is manipulation-class. All of them justify the discount we apply in valuation.

The cash-flow cross-check is less flattering and belongs in the report rather than a footnote. Free cash flow is negative in FY2026E at IDR-862.1bn because the land inventory absorbs working capital: the model carries operating working capital at a multiple of revenue, which for a developer is the land bank, so any growth year consumes cash before it produces it [S0, S2]. That is normal for this business model and it is why the RNAV method, not a free-cash-flow DCF, carries the valuation weight. What would make it abnormal is a growth year that consumes cash without a matching increase in customer advances, because that would mean land is being developed speculatively rather than sold forward [S2]. The earnings-quality screens come out clean on manipulation-class flags and amber on structure. Accruals are negative and large in both years the annual report carries a cash-flow statement: cash from operations of IDR2,402.4bn in FY2025 against group net profit of IDR857.1bn on average total assets of IDR15,056.2bn, and IDR1,870.0bn against IDR770.1bn the year before, so earnings ran behind cash rather than ahead of it [S2 p.136, p.9]. We give two years rather than three because the archived FY2025 annual report prints two comparative cash-flow years only, and we say so rather than extrapolating; the direction of the screen is unambiguous. Trade receivables fell while revenue rose, the opposite of the divergence flag we look for [S0]. The balance sheet carries debt of IDR4,606.5bn against equity of IDR6,263.6bn, net debt to EBITDA is 0.6, and the refinancing moved the whole dollar issue into rupiah on a long tenor [S0, S5]. The weakness is the minority leakage: of IDR857.1bn of group net profit only IDR423.2bn reached parent shareholders [S2]. Capital allocation has been conservative on dividends, with a payout of 10.0% [S0, S2].

The property template uses RNAV as the primary method at a 60% weight, with P/E and P/BV at 20% each on the company's own history. That mix fits an industrial-estate developer because reported earnings describe the land sold two years ago, while the value sits in the land still owned and the annuity of utilities attached to it. A pure earnings multiple on a company whose reported profit falls by a quarter on a one-off financing charge would be meaningless.

The cost of capital is 12.0% at a cost of equity of 21.0%, built from a risk-free rate of 7.4%, an equity risk premium of 4.2%, a country premium of 2.5% and a levered beta of 2.27 off an unlevered 0.90 [S0, house method]. The high cost of equity is the honest consequence of a leveraged developer in a balance-of-payments-stressed currency, and it is one penalty the model already carries before the discount.

The RNAV has three pieces. The land bank is marked on a monetisation basis: the Cikarang tranche that can be absorbed inside a decade at the FY2025 rate is valued at the achieved developed-land price less a stated haircut for the development spend and absorption risk, and the remainder is held at carrying cost because land beyond the horizon discounts to roughly book; Kendal's whole remaining area sits inside a short absorption window and is valued the same way; Tanjung Lesung is halved and Morotai is held at cost [S2]. That produces a land value of roughly twice the IDR5,783.5bn carrying value, not the many-fold number an appraisal would produce, and we say plainly that a full mark-to-market would be promoter math. Kendal is then cut to the group's attributable share, because PT Kawasan Industri Kendal is held 51.0% through a subsidiary and the balance is Sembcorp's: the minority's share of the Kendal uplift above book is deducted inside the land value, since the engine's RNAV is struck at the September balance-sheet date and deducts the minority interest carried at that date alongside September net debt [S0], of which IDR1,570.1bn sat in Kendal alone at the last audited year-end [S2 note 24]. Cikarang needs no cut - the estate is held through wholly owned entities and the group's minority book sits almost entirely in Kendal and the two residential joint ventures [S2]. The second piece capitalises recurring gross profit at 15.5%, which on the segment note's own margin is a low-double-digit yield on recurring EBIT and under ten times its EBITDA [S2]. The third piece deducts net debt at the September balance sheet and adds associates [S0].

The cap rate is the leg where we differ most from a generic property valuation, so here is the grid. On FY2026E recurring revenue of IDR2,977.7bn at the recurring gross margin, the house's mall cap rate - five points below the rate we hold - would value the recurring business about half as much again as we do; five points the other way would take roughly a quarter off. We hold 15.5%, the risk-adjusted industrial-utility rate in our assumptions, which capitalises recurring gross profit into the investment-property leg of the valuation table, because this is not prime Jakarta retail: it is Bekasi and Kendal industrial utility, a dry port, a golf course and a stalled tourism estate, and the power book is a take-or-pay capacity contract on a plant in cold reserve [S2 p.129]. The mall rate is the house default we reject here: a mall-grade yield is earned by lease covenants and rent rolls this segment does not have. The whole grid, including the mall-rate alternative and the value it would put on the leg, is printed in cap_rate_basis in the assumptions file, so the reader can see the leg rather than only our chosen point, and the deviation is carried as the name-specific judgement it is rather than as a house default [S2].

The cross-checks disagree, and the disagreement is the point. The P/E leg is Rp99, -38.6% below the RNAV leg, because the multiple is applied to current-year parent earnings that still carry the refinancing charge. Normalised instead on FY2027E parent earnings of IDR560.9bn, the same 9.9 gives a leg roughly two-thirds above the RNAV leg: the normalised cross-check brackets the primary from the other side rather than confirming it, and the engine's cross-check warning is that current-year-earnings artefact, not evidence that the land is worth less [S0, S2]. The multiple itself is the mean of the three year-ends in our own multiple history - the engine labels it a five-year average, but the series is shorter than that label and we treat it as a thin sample [S0]. The P/BV leg at Rp184 is closer, at 0.6 times a book value of Rp301 a share [S0]. We keep the earnings weight because a developer that cannot earn a return on book is not worth book, and we keep the RNAV weight because the land is the asset. The market currently prices the shares at 0.4x book and 3.4x EBITDA [S0], which is where asset-heavy, minority-heavy Indonesian developers sit when investors do not believe the asset.

The discount is the number the target is most sensitive to, so it is set from the name's own history rather than from a view about the market. On the RNAV per share in the valuation table, held constant across the series, the sixty-one monthly closes from November 2021 to November 2026 imply discounts ranging from the low sixties to the low eighties with a median near the middle of the seventies, and Rp120 today sits at the wide end of that band [S0]. We assume the discount returns to that median - a narrowing of about seven percentage points, not a move to the house sector band, which this name has never traded at [house card VAL_PROPERTY_DEVELOPER]. The reason to stop at the median is that we cannot source a dated catalyst for more: the refinancing is done [S5], the nine-month results are out [S3], and the house macro deck has the policy rate flat through FY2027E with IDR property on avoid [deck.macro], so there is no rate-cut re-rating to underwrite. The wide discount itself has three explained causes: minority leakage, a controller at 40.6% with a 54.9% free float [S0], and an absorption rate in Cikarang measured in the low tens of hectares a year [S2].

What today's price implies follows from that. At Rp120 the market is capitalising the shares at the wide end of the name's own five-year discount range: it pays for the recurring income stream and the book value of the land and assigns nothing to the development margin on built stock [S0, S2]. The expected return we publish rests on three drivers, none of which is a re-rating hope. The first is the refinancing: the dollar notes that carried the higher coupon and the currency mismatch are gone, swapped for a rupiah facility at a floating 7.0% [S5]. The second is earnings normalisation, with FY2027 parent profit recovering to IDR560.9bn once the one-off charge is out of the base [S3, S5]. The third is discount mean-reversion to 73.3%, inside the band the shares have traded in for five years [S0]. Nothing in that list requires the stock to trade at RNAV; it requires the price to stop assigning zero to land the company sold at IDR567.4bn for 18.0 ha last year [S2].

The three assumptions that move the answer are the land marking, the discount and the cap rate. A tenth of RNAV in the discount is worth more to the share price than a tenth of presales growth, because the multiple on asset value is where the leverage sits [S0]. We show the grid rather than a single point so the reader can see that even on bear-market land values the shares are not expensive, and that the target needs the discount to narrow, not the land to appreciate. The DCF printed in the next table is a cross-check on the recurring business only; it is not the primary method and we do not average it in, because a perpetual-growth model on a finite land bank flatters the terminal value and would double-count the land already marked in the RNAV [S0, S2].

The largest risk is that the land is worth less than the hectares suggest. Absorption in Cikarang has been in the low tens of hectares a year against a land bank of 1,152 ha there, and if Chinese and domestic manufacturers delay capex the tranche we mark up never sells [S2]. We rate this medium likelihood and high impact, and it is the driver we shock hardest in the bear case. Second, the new Central Java estates licensed in 2026 compete directly with Kendal and could compress the price per hectare we have held constant [S6] - medium likelihood, medium impact. Third, the rupiah: the currency mismatch has gone from the debt but not from the business, since industrial tenants and the land decision are dollar-linked; a renewed depreciation episode with the policy rate rising rather than falling would hit both [S2, deck.macro]. Fourth, governance and minority leakage: roughly half of group profit goes to minorities, related-party balances exist at the parent, and the collateral package on the new facility is comprehensive [S2, S5]. Fifth, liquidity and the share register: a 54.9% free float with insiders at 40.6% means the discount can persist longer than a fundamental case can stay solvent [S0].

We do not think a repeat of the 2026 charge is a risk to underwrite: the notes that caused it have been repaid and the new facility runs to a fifteen-year tenor [S5]. The genuine open question is the floating rate on that facility, and the bear case now takes it away. The IDR3,250.0bn is priced at a floating 7.0% for fifteen years against company and subsidiary assets at a collateral cover above the loan amount; the facility announcement gives the coupon, the tenor and the security but no repricing schedule, and we have not been able to source one [S5]. What we can test is the transmission: a hundred basis points on the drawn amount costs about an eighth of FY2026E financial expense and about a fifteenth of parent profit, and two hundred basis points about a quarter and an eighth. The bear case therefore carries a hundred basis points and the bull case the mirror image, so the rate path is priced rather than asserted.

Our bear case (probability 25%) is built to be a real downside: it cuts presales growth, takes a fifth off the land valuation, widens the discount to a level wider than today's, and adds a hundred basis points to the floating rate on the Mandiri facility. It values the shares at Rp140, which is above the price on a twelve-month view but below it on today's value, so the thesis is tested rather than flattered. The bull case (probability 25%) mirrors all four shocks - presales up, land marked up by a quarter, the discount at the narrow end of the name's own five-year band, and the floating rate a hundred basis points lower - giving Rp227. Base is Rp184 on a probability of 50%. Both cases shock the same four drivers by mirrored amounts; neither assumes full asset value, and the rate shock is a stress on a flat policy path rather than a forecast the house macro deck supports.

Interest coverage from recurring income only is the test the property card requires, and it is adequate but not comfortable. Recurring gross profit of the infrastructure pillar - power, water, dry port, estate services - covers the financial expense of IDR350.1bn more than twice over before any land is sold [S2 note 34, S0]. That is the profile of a developer whose annuity survives a presales winter; it is not a margin of safety against a two-hundred basis point repricing, which is why the rate shock sits in the scenario table rather than in a footnote.

Signposts that would change the view: a marketing-sales print below this year's run-rate; a Kendal price per hectare below the FY2025 achieved level; a decision to fund growth with new dollar debt again; and any related-party land transaction priced away from market.

Ownership is concentrated in the founder, who is also president director, with insiders at 40.6% and institutions at 17.9% [S0]. The board carries independent commissioners, and the audit committee reports no material internal-control weakness and no material legal exposure [S2]. The auditor is a BDO member firm on a first-period engagement; the audit fee is disclosed and no non-audit services were provided [S2]. The auditor's report page did not yield machine-readable text in our archived copy, so we state the auditor's identity and the committee's conclusion rather than characterise the opinion ourselves. IDX status we check first, because a special-monitoring-board listing would change every entry and exit assumption: KIJA trades on the exchange's main board with no special notation. The annual report's suspension and delisting disclosure records no suspension, no trading sanction and no delisting during FY2025 [S2 p.14], and no *papan pemantauan khusus* status or B/E/L/M/S notation letter appears in any document or press item we hold for the name [S2, S3, S4]. Continuous trading therefore applies, and the liquidity and exit assumptions are not exposed to a full call auction.

Related-party balances are disclosed at the parent level rather than buried, and are small against group revenue but a channel worth monitoring [S2]. The new bank facility is secured over company and subsidiary assets [S5] - normal for an Indonesian developer, but it ranks the secured lenders ahead of shareholders in any stress. Dividends have resumed: Rp2.03 a share for FY2025 against Rp1.77 the year before [S0, S2], a low payout that reflects the debt-reduction priority [S2].

Three structure checks we ran came back clean or explained. We found no disclosure of a pledge over the controlling shareholding in the annual report's shareholding section [S2]. There has been no rights issue in the period covered and no treasury-share placement beyond the earlier programme [S2]. And the audit relationship is new without an accompanying change in accounting policy, which is the combination that most often precedes a restatement [S2]. The remaining governance question is the one the structure creates rather than the people: with the founder as both controller and president director, related-party land transactions are the mechanism through which minority value could move, and the disclosure exists but the pricing of those transactions is not independently tested in the accounts [S2]. On ESG, the estate business is exposed to land-licensing and social risk at Tanjung Lesung and Morotai, and to the emissions profile of the tenants it supplies power to. The company publishes a sustainability report with the annual report and describes water, waste-water and estate-management investment as its environmental programme [S2]. We treat the environmental disclosure as adequate and the governance disclosure as better than the sector norm, while noting that a developer's appraisals are soft numbers and the related-party channel is where value would leak if it leaks at all.

The dated catalysts are the FY2026 marketing-sales print, the FY2026 audited accounts in which the refinanced interest line appears clean for the first time, and any Kendal phase-two conversion or data-centre tenant announcement in the first half of 2027 [S2, S5, S3]. Management guides to a much more conducive property market in 2027, and the first test of that guidance is the fourth-quarter sales number.

The KPIs we watch are the marketing-sales run-rate against the target [S2], the achieved price per hectare in Kendal against the FY2025 level [S2], recurring revenue growth from power and estate services [S3], the customer-advance balance as an indicator of how quickly land converts to revenue [S2], and the interest line once the rupiah facility has run a full year [S5]. A marketing-sales print below the current run-rate, or a Kendal price below the FY2025 achieved level, is the kill criterion for the view.

bear.narrative: Land absorption halves as Chinese and domestic manufacturers delay capex; the Rp11.9tn land-bank valuation is not earned, the discount stays near the current 80% because nothing re-rates a minority-heavy developer, and the floating rate on the Rp3.25tn Mandiri facility reprices 100bp higher as the rupiah stays under balance-of-payments pressure [S5, deck.macro].

bull.narrative: Data-centre, EV-battery and Chinese relocation demand lift Kendal and Cikarang absorption; the discount narrows within the name's own five-year band and the floating facility reprices 100bp lower as the Federal Reserve and BI ease together in FY2027 [S3, S2, S5].

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -33%: marketing sales were Rp1.52tn in 9M-2026 [S3] against a Rp3.75tn full-year target management set in the FY2025 report [S2 p.64], and management says buyers "cenderung lebih berhati-hati" [S3]; a Q4 in line with FY2025's Q4 gives c.Rp2.4tn, 33% below FY2025's Rp3.6tn [S2 p.123]. From FY2027E we assume cycle repair (+15%, +10%, +8%, +8%) off that trough: management guides to a "jauh lebih kondusif" 2027 [S3], and the nine-month 2026 transactions are named one by one - in Kendal a 9.7 ha household-appliance plant, a 7 ha Chinese battery producer and a 6 ha Chinese synthetic-leather producer, in Cikarang textile, power and Chinese building-material buyers [S3]. We do NOT read S6 as reassurance about Bekasi: the twelve new Central Java industrial estates it reports include Kendal and Batang, so it is competition for the growth engine, and that is why recovery is 15% rather than the +12%/+13% swings of FY2024-FY2025 and why the land valuation holds the FY2025 Kendal price rather than lifting it.

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: 0.9. Customer advances of Rp1,021.7bn at 31 Dec 2025 [S2 p.135] are only 28% of FY2025 presales, so most contracted land is recognised inside twelve months; the LK also shows the FY2026 land-sale revenue being pulled forward (9M-2026 Land Development revenue Rp1,914.8bn against Rp974.9bn in H1 alone) [S3]. One-to-two-year recognition lag on the high-rise and residential tail keeps this below 1.0.

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +16%: the infrastructure pillar earned Rp2,242.5bn in 9M-2026, 53% of revenue, with electricity at Rp1,505.2bn and services up 33% to Rp525.6bn [S3]; adding a Q4 in line with FY2025 gives c.Rp3.0tn against Rp2,567bn in FY2025 [S2 p.11]. The deceleration to 10%, 9%, 8%, 8% and then 5% is a capacity limit, not a view on demand: the power book is a single 130 MW plant at Cikarang whose sale to PLN runs on a take-or-pay contract and which has been in PLN reserve shutdown [S2 p.127, p.46], so electricity revenue grows by billed volume and tariff on that installed capacity, while the faster-growing services line (dry port, water, waste water, estate management) starts from Rp525.6bn and cannot carry a Rp3tn pillar on its own at 30% a year. No new generating capacity is assumed beyond the announced Kendal WTP/WWTP and mini-LNG additions [S2 p.129].

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 48.3% is the rate the nine months actually realised: reported 9M-2026 gross profit of Rp1,577.8bn on revenue of Rp4,254.9bn is a 37.1% group margin [S3], and applying the FY2025 segment margins to the nine-month mix (development Rp2,012.4bn, recurring Rp2,242.5bn) would give 38.8%, so the development pillar earned 48.3% in the period, 3.6pp below FY2025. That compression is the price of the weak cycle, not a new level: FY2027E onward returns to 52%, the rate the audited segment note shows for both FY2025 (51.9%) and FY2024 (51.9%) [S2 note 34], as the sold mix shifts back towards ready industrial land in Cikarang priced at the FY2025 achieved level. No margin expansion beyond the last audited actual is assumed.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: 27%, the FY2025 infrastructure-pillar gross margin (power generation Rp325.1bn on Rp1,818.1bn of revenue, 17.9%; services and maintenance Rp367.6bn on Rp797.6bn, 46.1%), down from 30% in FY2024 as the low-margin electricity resale grew 54% [S2 p.51, note 34]. The same base is capitalised in the RNAV, so the P&L and the balance-sheet valuation stay consistent.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: 15.5% of recurring gross profit, equal to a 10.3% yield on recurring segment EBIT and 7.9x EV/EBITDA - see cap_rate_basis in params. Justified by asset quality (industrial utilities and dry port in Bekasi and Kendal, golf and a stalled tourism estate at Tanjung Lesung) and by the PLN cold-reserve capacity contract behind the power book [S2 p.129].

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: 73.3%, the median of the name's own five-year constant-RNAV discount series. On a constant RNAV of Rp602 a share (after the minority share is netted out of the land value), the sixty-one monthly closes from November 2021 to November 2026 imply a discount range of 62.1% to 82.1%, a median of 73.3% and a current reading of 80.1% at Rp120 [S0 price history, own RNAV]. We assume reversion to that median, i.e. a 7pp narrowing from today, which is the most probable point of a series that has spent five years returning to its middle; the house sector band of 40-70% [house card VAL_PROPERTY_DEVELOPER] is not reached because the name has never traded there. There is no rate-cut catalyst to justify more: the house macro deck carries the policy rate flat at 5.75 through FY2027E and puts IDR property on AVOID, so a discount at the bottom of the name's history would rest on an unsourced re-rating. The discount still exceeds the sector band because minorities take 50.6% of FY2025 net profit [S2 note 24], the controller holds 40.6% with a 54.9% free float [S0], and Cikarang absorption is about 21 ha a year.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 12.6%, the audited FY2025 charge: selling expenses Rp68.2bn plus general and administrative Rp580.9bn on revenue of Rp5,149.4bn [S2 p.121-123]. The engine's EBIT line takes selling and G&A only, so the ratio used must be that 12.6% and not a higher figure that would smuggle an unallocated cost into opex; at 14.1% the FY2025 re-run understated EBITDA by 2.54pp against the reported margin, which is the calibration gap this fixes. Held flat because estate overhead scales with the number of tenants, not with land revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: restated from the LK: FY2025 D&A of Rp187.6bn (segment note 34, all segments) on Rp5,149.4bn of revenue is 3.64%, against the data pack line of Rp18.3bn; FY2024 was Rp193.0bn. Set to the FY2025 actual.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capital expenditure of Rp206.0bn on Rp5,149.4bn of revenue is 4.0%; the three-year average is 5.7% (FY2024 Rp342.5bn on utility build-out). We hold the FY2025 actual, since the announced Kendal WTP/WWTP, mini-LNG and FCR projects are inside the land-development budget rather than incremental.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default 1.5x revenue, which for a developer is the land and inventory balance rather than trade working capital; kept at the default so the FCFF cross-check charges the company for carrying its land bank

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 LK: income tax of Rp104.4bn on Rp961.5bn of pre-tax profit is 10.9% (FY2024 6.2%) - property developers pay a final 2.5% on land and building transfers and the rest at the standard rate; we use the three-year average of 10%.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 7.6% blended. The Rp3.25tn Bank Mandiri facility signed 13 May 2026 carries a floating 7% on a 15-year tenor and refinances the US$185.9m Senior Notes that paid 8% stepping to 9% [S5, S2 p.14]; the remaining bank loans cost roughly 9%. That is below the 9.1% the LK shows for FY2025 (financial expenses Rp420.1bn on average debt), which is why the refinancing is earnings-accretive despite the one-off charge.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 LK financial income of Rp124.8bn on opening cash of Rp2,048.5bn is 6.1%; held at 6% rather than the pack default of 7%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: zero: the refinancing swapped the instrument, not the amount, and FY2025 debt of Rp4,606.5bn is unchanged at Rp4,863.8bn at 30 Sep 2026; management guides to extending tenor and reducing the debt burden, not to new leverage

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -518: the size that reproduces the reported nine months plus a fourth quarter at the FY2025 fourth-quarter level. Nine-month net profit was Rp391.7bn against Rp634.6bn a year earlier, the fall being the one-off refinancing charge booked in Q2-2026 (FX loss on settling the dollar notes, hedge-termination cost, accelerated amortisation) [S3, S4]; the Q2 parent swing was -Rp235.7bn against +Rp267.4bn [S0]. Because that charge is inside the nine months, the fourth quarter should be no weaker than Q4-2025's Rp222.5bn, and the remaining FY2026E other charge is the group-level FX and hedge cost. From FY2027E we hold -Rp127bn, the FY2025A audited run-rate (history: -475, -247, -203, -127) [S0, S2], because hedge costs, write-offs and non-operating FX on the residual dollar items do not disappear when the notes are repaid; assuming zero would be an unsourced permanent uplift of roughly Rp50-100bn of parent profit a year.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 48%: FY2025 minorities took Rp433.9bn of Rp857.1bn (50.6%) and FY2024 52.8%; the FY2023 level was 42%.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: the FY2025 dividend of Rp2.0349 a share paid in June 2026 is Rp42.4bn, 10% of FY2025 parent net profit of Rp423.2bn; the FY2024 payout was Rp36.3bn.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 0%: 20,824,888,369 shares issued, of which 28.1m are treasury stock, unchanged since the FY2024 treasury sale; no rights issue has been announced.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: house terminal growth for IDR: 4%, below the long-run nominal GDP path in the macro deck, applied to a business whose land bank is finite.

challenges.challenge: The third named driver of the +104% is RNAV-discount mean-reversion to 65% (fund record:159-161 cites 'the BI path turns down into FY2027 [macro deck]' as a dated catalyst). The house macro deck has bi_rate 5.75 spot and 5.75 FY2027E - flat, not falling - and puts INDO rate-sensitive names including property on AVOID. Section 2 compounds it by printing 'the policy rate easing into FY2027E at 575.0%'. Moving the discount from the current implied 82% to 65% is worth 685.5 x 0.17 = Rp117/share of RNAV, Rp70 of the blend and Rp85 of the Rp243 target - 35% of it - on a citation that does not say what the report claims. The second cited catalyst, the May-2026 Mandiri refinancing, is a completed event, and 'inside the band the shares themselves established this year' is unverifiable because no own-5y discount series is shown.
challenges.answer: Discount is now 73.3%, the median of this name own five-year constant-RNAV series over 61 monthly closes (range 62.1% to 82.1%, current reading 80.1%), not a 16pp narrowing; no rate-cut catalyst is claimed and the flat BI path plus the property-sector avoid call are printed in sections 2 and 4. Target falls from Rp243 to Rp184 and expected return from 103.8% to 54.3%, rating stays BUY [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: The bear scenario values the shares at Rp184, 53% above the Rp120 price, so no probability-weighted outcome tests the thesis. Its narrative at fund record:363-364 says 'the RNAV discount stays near the market's current level', but the shock at lines 376-378 adds only 0.10 to a 0.65 base (75%), not the 82% implied today. The bear touches only presales growth, recurring growth, landbank and discount: it never shocks cost_of_debt, gross margin or absorption duration, and section 5 concedes 'the bear case does not take that benefit away' on the floating rate.
challenges.answer: Bear rebuilt: discount +10pp to 83.3% (wider than the current 80.1%), land -20%, presales -15pp and cost_of_debt +100bp on the floating Mandiri facility. Bear target Rp140.4 against the Rp120 price, and its value before the twelve-month roll is Rp116.9, below the price; section 5 says so plainly instead of presenting a flattering bear [S5][S2].

challenges.challenge: The RNAV bridge deducts minority interest at book, Rp1,810bn, while section 1 concludes 'any valuation of the land has to travel through that minority share' and section 3 says minorities took 50.6% of FY2025 profit on a book of Rp1,880.8bn (two different figures). Kendal alone contributes Rp3,543bn of the Rp6,158bn uplift of land value over book (4,290 vs 747), and Cikarang and Kendal sit in subsidiaries with significant minority holders, so a proportional deduction is larger than book. Every Rp1tn of under-deduction is Rp48/share of RNAV and about Rp10 of the target.
challenges.answer: Kendal is 51% group and 49% Sembcorp [S2 p.549]; the minority share of the Kendal uplift above book (Rp1,736bn of Rp3,543bn) is deducted inside params.landbank_value, cutting RNAV per share to about Rp602. The 1,810 vs 1,880.8 gap is date not scope: the engine deducts the 30 Sep 2026 minority balance while 1,880.8 is the 31 Dec 2025 LK figure [S2 p.120], reconciled in valuation.post_bs_review.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E is not bridged to the reported 9M-2026. On the model lines: revenue 5,508.5 vs 4,254.9 reported implies Q4 revenue of 1,253.6, -15% on Q4-2025's 1,474.7; gross profit 2,120.0 vs 1,577.8 implies a 43.2% Q4 gross margin against 37.1% for the nine months; EBITDA 1,541.3 vs 1,362.4 implies Q4 EBITDA of 178.9, a 14.3% margin against 32.0%; and group net profit 430.2 vs 391.7 implies Q4 of +38.5bn against Q4-2025's +222.5bn. No source supports a Q4 that is simultaneously the highest-margin and lowest-EBITDA quarter of the year, and the shallow FY2026E base is what makes the FY2027E recovery read as +156%.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is bridged line by line to the reported nine months on revenue, gross profit, EBIT, finance cost, other, tax and minorities; the development gross margin falls to the 9M realised rate so Q4 needs no margin jump, and other_nonop is recalibrated to -518 so group net profit equals the 9M figure plus a Q4 no weaker than FY2025 Q4. The 9M EBITDA print is flagged as a different company definition implying SG&A near a twentieth of revenue [S3][S4][S2].

challenges.challenge: other_nonop is set to exactly 0.0 from FY2027E to FY2035E (engine history -475.2, -247.1, -203.2 and -127.0 in FY2022A-FY2025A), while the analyst's own basis for the -730 FY2026E figure says it includes 'the other-expense run-rate'. Removing a four-year average of -263bn, or even just the FY2025A -127bn, is an unsourced permanent uplift of roughly Rp50-100bn of parent net profit a year from FY2027E and is a material part of why parent NP rises 156% on a 9% revenue increase.
challenges.answer: other_nonop now holds -127 from FY2027E to the long run, the FY2025A audited run-rate, instead of zeroing; the basis explains that hedge costs and non-operating FX survive the note repayment. FY2027E parent profit and the P/E leg are restated on that lower base [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: S3 reports 9M-2026 consolidated gross profit of Rp1,577.8bn, up 7% from Rp1,472.8bn, on revenue up 16% - a gross margin of 37.1%, down from 40.1%. Section 3 reports only FY2025's 39.5% and never mentions the 9M compression, so the reader is told the profit fall is entirely a refinancing charge when 3.0pp of gross-margin compression is also in the reported numbers. The model's FY2026E gross margin is 38.5% (2,120.0/5,508.5), 1.4pp above the latest actual, and its Q4 needs 43.2%.
challenges.answer: Section 3 prints the 9M-2026 group gross margin and decomposes the fall into mix (electricity resale at 17.9% growing more than half, against 51.9% on land) rather than price, says the recurring 27% is a floor, and carries 48.3% on development in FY2026E - the realised nine-month rate - reverting to the audited 51.9% from FY2027E [S3][S2].

challenges.challenge: The whole re-rating rests on a 15-year floating 7% rupiah facility of Rp3.25tn secured at 120% over company and subsidiary assets, i.e. over the land the RNAV marks up, and no scenario shocks the rate. The house deck has the rupiah under balance-of-payments pressure with the policy rate flat at 5.75 through FY2027, so a rising-rate path is plausible, and section 5 itself names the risk while leaving it out of the bear. The report also gives no interest coverage from recurring income, which the property method card requires.
challenges.answer: cost_of_debt moves +100bp in the bear and -100bp in the bull on the floating facility, and section 5 quantifies transmission: 100bp is about an eighth of financial expense and a fifteenth of parent profit, 200bp about a quarter and an eighth. The facility announcement publishes coupon, tenor and collateral cover but no repricing schedule, stated rather than invented [S5].

challenges.challenge: The recurring annuity is capitalised at 15.5% of gross profit, about 9.6x segment EBIT and 7.9x EBITDA, and the report expressly rejects the 10.5% mall cap rate it says the house uses for PWON without ever valuing the alternative. At 10.5% the investment-property piece is about Rp8.3tn rather than Rp5.64tn, adding about Rp129/share of RNAV, Rp45 of the RNAV leg, Rp27 of the blend and Rp33 of the target - roughly 13% of the published Rp243 - on a segment with a PLN take-or-pay contract and named data-centre tenants. Understating a defensible bull leg is as wrong as overstating the bear.
challenges.answer: Cap-rate grid published in cap_rate_basis (10.5% gives 8,326; 12% gives 7,286; 13.5% gives 6,477; 15.5% gives 5,640; 18% gives 4,857) and section 4 states the alternative, why the mall rate is not taken on a golf course, a stalled tourism estate and a cold-reserve capacity contract, and what the spread is worth. The engine sensitivity pair is fixed in the industry config, so the grid sits in the input basis [S2].

challenges.challenge: recurring_growth decays from 16% to 10/9/8/8% and then 5%, with terminal growth 4%, even though the infrastructure pillar grew 54% in electricity and 33% in services in FY2025, is now 53% of revenue, and the report names data-centre, EV-battery and Chinese relocation demand as the pipeline. No sensitivity or source supports the deceleration from FY2030, and the 4% terminal sits on a business the report says has a finite land bank but an annuity-like utility book.
challenges.answer: Deceleration is sourced to capacity not demand: the power book is a single 130 MW Bekasi Power plant, wholly owned, on a PLN take-or-pay contract in reserve shutdown [S2 p.127], so electricity revenue grows on billed volume rather than new capacity, and the faster services line cannot carry the pillar at 30% a year. Recurring-growth sensitivity is shown through the mirrored scenario shocks because the engine pair is config-fixed [S2][S3].

challenges.challenge: The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract is not met: there is no three-year accruals ratio (the report asserts 'accruals are negative in each year we can compute' with no numbers), and related-party flows are described only as 'set out in the parent-company accounts [S2]' rather than quantified as % of revenue and assets, which the card calls the modal value-destruction channel on IDX. The cash_yield basis is also internally inconsistent: 6.1% is computed on 'opening cash of Rp2,048.5bn', but FY2025 net debt of Rp985.5bn against debt of Rp4,606.5bn implies closing cash near Rp3,621bn and a realised average yield of about 4.4%.
challenges.answer: Accruals now carry numbers: FY2025 cash from operations 2,402.4 against group net profit 857.1 on average total assets 15,056.2, and FY2024 1,870.0 against 770.1 [S2 p.136, p.9]; two years rather than three because the archived annual report prints two comparative cash-flow years, and we say so. Related-party balances are quantified (174.5 receivables, 228.0 payables) as shares of revenue and assets [S2 p.573-574].

challenges.challenge: opex_pct is 0.141 but its own basis text says 'the same 12.6% the engine uses [S0, S2]' - a 1.5pp unexplained wedge, worth about Rp77bn of EBITDA a year, which is exactly the scale of the calibration gate's -2.54pp gap (model FY2025A EBITDA margin 27.98% vs actual 30.52%). The gate is not answered in qc_justifications, and the same under-run is carried for a decade: FY2026E-FY2035E EBITDA margin is about 28% against a 9M-2026 actual of 32.0% (1,362.4/4,254.9).
challenges.answer: opex_pct is now 12.6%, the audited FY2025 selling plus G&A charge on revenue, replacing the 14.1% engine default whose own basis text already said 12.6%; the wedge was worth about 77bn of EBITDA a year. That removes the FY2025 margin under-run: the calibration gap is now 2.7pp and driven only by the FY2026 gross-mix change, sourced to the 9M print [S2][S3].

challenges.challenge: Unit and basis errors undermine verifiability: section 2 prints 'the policy rate easing into FY2027E at 575.0%' (5.75%), the text repeatedly renders units as 'RpIDR...bnbn' and 'ha hectares', and section 5 prints 'bear case (probability 0.2%)' and 'Base ... 0.5%' against 25%/50% in fund record. The summary also reports 9M 'net profit of Rp391.7bn' without saying parent or consolidated - the distinction decides whether FY2026E parent NP of Rp223.7bn implies a Q4 loss.
challenges.answer: Units fixed throughout (IDR bn not doubled with Rp or bn, hectares not doubled), the policy-rate line reads flat at 5.75 percent through FY2027E on a raw placeholder instead of 575.0%, and the scenario probabilities resolve from the model at 25/50/25. The 391.7 nine-month figure is consolidated net profit, not parent, and section 3 shows the implied Q4 on that basis [S3].

challenges.challenge: The presales basis (fund record:47-51) argues the twelve new Central Java estates are 'competition only in Central Java, not in its Bekasi base [S6]', but S6 lists Kendal and Batang by name and Kendal is KIJA's growth engine and about 58% of the RNAV uplift; the same basis then assumes presales recover +15% in FY2027 from a -33% FY2026 trough. S6 is dated 2026-11-11, four days before the model was built.
challenges.answer: S6 is cited two-sided: the twelve new Central Java estates include Kendal and Batang, so they compete with the growth engine; that is why FY2027E recovery is +15% rather than the 12% to 13% swings of FY2024-25 and why the Kendal land price is held at FY2025 rather than lifted. The 2026 transactions behind the recovery are named from S3 [S6][S3].

missing_bull_case.note: The utility annuity is capitalised at 15.5% of gross profit and the 10.5% alternative is dismissed without being valued (C8); recurring growth decays to 5% and terminal 4% despite the pillar growing 54% in FY2025 (C9). Neither upside is quantified in a grid.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear is Rp184, 53% above the Rp120 price, and its narrative (discount stays near market) contradicts its own +10pp shock; no scenario shocks cost_of_debt, gross margin or absorption duration (C2, C7). A bearer of the risk would not recognise this distribution.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E is not bridged to the reported 9M-2026 and implies a Q4 with a 43.2% gross margin and a 14.3% EBITDA margin (C4); other_nonop is set to zero from FY2027E against a four-year average of -263bn (C5); FY2027 presales +15% ignores the twelve new Kendal/Batang estates in S6 (C13).

evidence_and_citations.note: S5/S3/S4 support the 7% facility, the one-off components and the temporary framing, so the core thesis is sourced. But the 9M gross margin of 37.1% is omitted (C6) and the earnings-quality output contract - 3y accruals ratio and related-party % of revenue/assets - is asserted rather than computed (C10).

valuation_method_fit.note: RNAV is the right primary method at the right weight and the land haircuts are stated, but the discount-narrowing leg has no forward catalyst the cited deck supports (C1) and the minority bridge deducts book value, not the minority share of the land uplift the report itself warns about (C3).

bias_and_tone.note: The prose repeatedly says the market assigns nothing to the land and that even the bear is far above the price, which overstates the evidential reach of a 65% discount chosen inside a 40-70% band; plus unit and probability formatting errors (C12). The conclusion would survive a lower discount, but at roughly a third of the published upside.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Inconsistent with the macro deck: bi_rate is 5.75 spot and 5.75 FY2027E (flat) and INDO property is on AVOID, yet section 2 and 4 turn this into easing and a tailwind (C1). The deck's usd_idr 18,350 is nowhere in the model, and S5 converts the notes at 17,500, so the rupiah principal is understated.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative: opex_pct 14.1% against the LK's 12.6% that the same basis cites (C11); capex 4.5% vs a 5.7% three-year average; FY2026 presales 2.4tn vs management's 3.75tn target, though the 9M arithmetic supports it. Optimistic: other_nonop zeroed from FY2027E (C5), cash_yield 6% vs a 4.4% realised average. Landbank shocks 0.8/1.25 are reciprocal, so mirrored.

calibration.note: The calibration gate shows FY2025A EBITDA margin 27.98% against an actual 30.52%, a -2.54pp gap with no qc_justification, and the model holds -4.0pp against the 9M-2026 actual of 32.0%. flags.message: a.dev_gross_margin moves +3.7pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The +3.7pp is a return to the last audited actual, not an expansion beyond it: the segment note shows a 51.9% real-estate gross margin in both FY2024 and FY2025 [S2 note 34], and FY2026E is the only year set below that, at the 48.3% rate the reported nine-month gross profit of Rp1,577.8bn on Rp4,254.9bn of revenue implies [S3]. Holding the trough for a decade would be an unsourced permanent margin cut on a pillar that sold land at the FY2025 achieved price.

flags.message: expected return +54%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The +54% expected return is built from drivers that are either already realised or inside the name's own history, not from a re-rating hope: (i) the 13 May 2026 Mandiri refinancing replaced the US$185.9m dollar notes paying 8-9% with a 15-year rupiah facility at a floating 7%, so the FY2025 financial-expense run-rate and the hedge and accelerated-amortisation drag do not recur [S5, S2]; (ii) earnings normalise as the FY2026 one-off, booked in Q2 and therefore inside the reported nine months, rolls out of the base - FY2027E parent profit against the FY2026E figure that already absorbs it [S3, S4]; (iii) the RNAV discount narrows to its own five-year median of 73.3%, against 80.1% implied by today's price on a constant-RNAV series that has ranged from 62.1% to 82.1% since November 2021 [S0]. Today's price of Rp120 implies that 80.1% discount: the market pays for the recurring income and the book value of the land and nothing for the development margin the company realised at Rp31.5bn a hectare in Cikarang in FY2025 [S2].
